author: Codex source-review pass
limitations: Complete raw-site review for Leviticus-Triage/llm-honeypot-intelligence at the frozen 20-r2 pin only; it does not close P2.
The same model performed the author and second source-review passes; this is not independent human annotation.
Two adopted questions establish source-level candidates only. The local replay did not inspect real generated artifacts, expose private addresses, use a live Tor daemon, or transmit a report.
The repo source shows Docker-volume inputs and a configured GitHub push, but this review does not establish that the upstream repository is public or that any private address was actually committed.

reviews.rationale: The literal CRON_MARKER is used only to find a legacy operator crontab line before removal. A false positive could remove a similarly named cron line, but this match does not validate attacker input or enforce a security policy.

review_refs.why: matching lines are removed from the operator crontab

reviews.rationale: The same literal CRON_MARKER is used in grep -v to remove the legacy scheduled job. This is operator configuration maintenance; its broad substring behavior is not a security-boundary property.

review_refs.why: marker determines whether cron rewrite runs

reviews.rationale: The awk pattern extracts the Hostname field from ssh -G output to display/connect to the configured T-Pot destination. The target comes from operator SSH configuration, and no authorization or sanitizer guarantee is attached to this regex.

review_refs.why: ssh configuration is converted into the destination host

reviews.rationale: The awk pattern selects MemTotal from /proc/meminfo to calculate an informational hardware warning. It is not an input validator or security control.

review_refs.why: procfs value feeds the memory display

reviews.rationale: The awk pattern selects IdentityFile entries from local ssh -G output; the caller then checks whether a configured file exists. This is operator SSH configuration handling and has no regex-specific security guarantee in this call path.

review_refs.why: helper resolves identity from local SSH config
IdentityFile output is consumed by the loop

reviews.rationale: The ERE looks for Elasticsearch or T-Pot names in docker ps output to produce an operator health message. It is a status check and print path, not an access decision or security sanitizer.

review_refs.why: match only emits a health message

reviews.rationale: set_kv receives four fixed internal key names at its call sites and uses grep to decide whether to append or replace an operator-edited dotenv entry. The key is not untrusted pattern input and the regex does not enforce a trust boundary.

The sed expression is built from the same fixed internal set_kv keys and updates an operator configuration file. Its value interpolation may affect edit correctness, but that is not a regex-based security-boundary guarantee at this site.

review_refs.why: key and value are helper parameters
callers pass the fixed key set

reviews.rationale: This ERE selects configured LLM endpoint/model keys for display after the fixed set_kv calls. It is presentation filtering, not input validation or access control.

review_refs.why: selected entries are printed for operator review

reviews.rationale: The IPv4-shaped ERE computes a count that is written to the sync log. File copying and remote synchronization proceed independently; the match neither validates the blocklist nor gates blocking behavior.

review_refs.why: count is only included in a log message

reviews.rationale: The substring ERE counts CSV rows for an operator log. The file itself is still synchronized; no row is admitted, rejected, or treated as trusted based on this count.

review_refs.why: file sync is independent of count

reviews.rationale: The pinned script calls this helper a private-IP sanitizer, applies it to generated rules and threat-intelligence files copied from Docker volumes, then commits/pushes those artifacts. RFC 1918 gives an independent domain for private IPv4 addresses. The formal counterexample is one unredacted 10/8 token; the exact pinned helper replay confirms representative 10/8 and 172.16/12 values remain unchanged. No real generated data or repository publication was inspected.

The pattern checks a field substring in the HTTPS check.torproject.org JSON response and only prints a diagnostic. It is not used to classify user-controlled data or to select a security-sensitive route.

review_refs.why: external Tor status field is checked

reviews.rationale: The pattern checks the expected Tor-project JSON marker during startup before the firewall setup. The response comes from the HTTPS bootstrap probe; this regex is a readiness heuristic, not the egress enforcement rule itself. The exact status parser is not claimed to validate arbitrary response bodies.

The pattern looks for the interface state in ip link output to decide whether to attempt bringing the configured interface up. It is a recovery/status branch; the configured interface and command output are local operator/system state.

review_refs.why: state match only suppresses an ip-link repair attempt

reviews.rationale: The helper sends AUTHENTICATE, SIGNAL NEWNYM, and QUIT together, then searches the complete response stream for 250 OK. A successful authentication reply followed by a 551/552 signal error therefore returns success. The exact pinned function reproduced this with a local fake nc response; no live Tor instance or scan deployment was used.

review_refs.why: grep status is logged as signal success
rotator liveness is enforced by watchdog
